liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Clementine** (4 reviews): Singled out as the highlight: a jazzy performance played as a shuffle; A slower, shuffled version that the reviewer finds jazzy and sublime [4][6][8][10]
- **Spanish Jam** (4 reviews): The jam is cut in this copy; the tracks after it are likely from 9/20/68; The reviewer thinks it sounds more Middle-Eastern than Spanish [4][11][12][13]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): An early version with alternate second-verse lyrics; The Cowboy Neal lyrics appear here in January, though the reviewer thought they followed Cassady's February 1968 death [8][14]
- **New Potato Caboose** (1 other source): A reel flip occurs during this song [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Clementine**: rare: 7 archived performances [15]
- **Born Cross Eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [15]
- **Drum Solo w/ unknown Tabla Artist**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- Earliest performances in the archive: St Stephen [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-01-23.sbd.finney.4528.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 72 min; rated 2/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: The Finney soundboard has some mix issues, though the sound quality is strong overall [4]
- **gd1968-01-23.sbd.miller.97343.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 5 songs; 32 min; rated 4.19/5 by 16 [2]. Said about its sound: Phil sits a bit low in the mix, and the Spanish Jam is cut [6]

## Around the show

- The reviewer argues this show and the one labeled the 22nd were really played on the 26th and 27th at Eagles [13]
- The performances are compared to the material on the album Anthem of the Sun [5]
- The reviewer ranks the upgraded source among the top ten shows of 1968 [6]
- New Potato Caboose here is judged probably one of the best of 1968 [8]
- Country Joe & the Fish did a similar jam that year, calling it Eastern Jam [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-01-23.sbd.finney.4528.shnf**: transferred by D Finney; source: Soundboard > MC > R > DAT > CDR [1]. Also: Listed as possibly a duplicate of 1/22/68, because the setlist looks similar and DeadBase XI has no 1/23/68 entry; Contributors credited are David Sorochty and DeadBase XI [1]
- **gd1968-01-23.sbd.miller.97343.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: This transfer comes from a DAT supplied by Rob Eaton; Pitch correction was applied, with help from Joe B. Jones [2]
